text:
Natalie R: @here found a potentially serious RBAC regression in the Console. Viewer accounts can create API keys via Settings > API keys UI. Repro steps and quick notes below, please triage.

Samir: thanks for the flag. can you drop repro + request/response? priority?

Natalie R: repro steps:
1) sign in as user with role=viewer
2) navigate to /console/settings/api-keys
3) click Create API key -> name -> Create
4) UI shows success, new key visible

curl example (from a test viewer):
```
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer <viewer_token>" \
  https://console.redwood.ai/api/v1/orgs/123/api-keys \
  -d '{"name":"tmp-by-viewer"}'
```
response: 201 Created, body contains key

Samir: whoa. sounds like backend isn't enforcing role check, front-end gating only. can you paste server logs for that request (id/trace)?

Natalie R: log snippet from api-server (redacted):
```
[2026-01-11T15:13:40Z] TRACE request_id=req_0a1b2c user_id=u_987 role=viewer path=/api/v1/orgs/123/api-keys method=POST status=201 duration_ms=42
```
It literally logged role=viewer and status=201.

sec-bot: alert: privilege-escalation-detection: high - API_KEY_CREATED_BY_NON_PRIVILEGED (https://alerts.redwood.ai/ALERT-3421)

Lee T: tagging this P0. remediation options:
- patch server middleware to enforce `can_create_api_key` check and return 403
- roll back frontend create button (low friction)
- bulk revoke keys created by viewers and rotate affected secrets

Mike C: confirmed repro locally on staging. quick curl returns 201, server handler uses `hasOrgPermission` but the org-perm mapping changed after recent role-matrix refactor (editor/viewer split). looks like `create_api_key` was moved to a new permission name `api_keys.create` and the mapping for viewer wasn't updated, but the code path defaults to allow if mapping missing.

Samir: ok that explains it. immediate mitigations: disable endpoint via feature flag or change default deny. I'll open a hotfix PR to add explicit deny when permission lookup returns null.

Natalie R: I've started a script to list keys created in last 48h by non-admins: `python tools/list_apikeys.py --since 48h --role viewer,editor` and will paste results in followup. Also created an Audit ticket and CC'd Compliance.

ops-bot: deploy scheduled: patch-rbac-default-deny -> canary @ 15:30 UTC

Lee T: we should also check KMS audit logs for wrapping/unwrapping usage for those keys. if any viewer-created keys were used to access customer data, escalate to incident response. @Samir can you check KMS logs and mark any hits?

Samir: on it. pulling KMS audit for key creation events (kms:CreateKey / keyAlias creation). will correlate key IDs from list.

sec-bot: note: make sure to save the original audit trail - do not delete any logs. compliance requires full chain.

Mike C: PR opened -> https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/4123
- adds server-side permission check
- default deny when permission missing
- unit tests

Natalie R: initial scan: 7 keys created by viewer-role accounts in last 24h. rotating those now and notifying owners. adding revocation runbook steps to the ticket.

Lee T: good. next actions: (1) monitor canary deploy, (2) revoke/rotate affected keys, (3) KMS audit correlation, (4) follow incident if any unauthorized access found. assign owners: Samir(KMS + hotfix), Natalie(revocation + compliance), Mike(PR + tests), Lee(incident lead)

Samir: will post trace IDs and KMS correlation by EOD.

Natalie R: thanks team. small ask: add a lint rule to fail CI if permission mapping contains a missing mapping that would default to allow.

Mike C: adding that to the PR.

Lee T: thumbs up. keep updates here, we'll move to incident channel if we see data access. :thumbsup:

Natalie R: updating ticket with canary progress now. thanks everyone.
